name: Winding temperature indicator
summary: Transformer indicator that adds a CT-heated thermal image to top-oil temperature to estimate winding hot-spot temperature.
description: A winding temperature indicator estimates transformer winding hot-spot temperature, which cannot easily be measured directly. A sensor in the top-oil pocket is heated by a small element fed from a CT on the load current, so the reading rises with both oil temperature and load, and its contacts control fans and give alarm and trip.

The schematic should show the CT feeding the heater, the calibration resistor and each contact stage. The symbol does not show the thermal gradient setting, which must be adjusted to the transformer heat-run data for the reading to be meaningful.
readingNotes: Trace the CT circuit feeding the thermal image heater.
Identify contact stages for cooling, alarm and trip.
distinction: A WTI estimates winding hot-spot with a thermal image; an oil temperature indicator reads oil temperature only.
